full_judgment:
"Let a Rule Nisi be issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why order being No. 146 dated 27-9-2017 passed by the learned Judge of Artha Rin Adalat, Laimonirhat in Artha Rin Decree Execution Case No. 17 of 2003 arising out of Artha Rin Suit No. 17 of 2000 (Annexure-H series) cancelling registered Boinama Deed No. 2409 dated 20-6-2013 executed and registered in the name of the petitioner with a direction upon Respondent No. 2 to make entry in Balam Bohi regarding cancellation of aforesaid Boinama Deed and also directing the petitioner to take return of BD (Bank Draft) should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and of no legal effect and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper." 

 2. Relevant facts leading to issuance of the Rule Nisi are that the respondent-Bank, namely, Pubali Bank Limited obtained a decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, Lalmonirhat in Artha Rin Suit No. 17 of 2000 for Taka 4,56,414 with up-to-date interest (decree signed on 29-5-2001). Accordingly, the decree-holder Bank filed Artha Rin Execution Case No. 17 of 2003 for Taka 5,86.988. 

 3. In the execution proceeding, the mortgaged property was put on auction and the present petitioner as highest bidder purchased the said property. Regarding sale, entire payment of Taka 20 lac having been paid on 26-6-2013, the Adalat directed to issue Boinama and it was registered on 28-6-2013. The Adalat also disposed of the execution case with satisfaction in accordance with section 33(9) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 ("the Act, 2003"). 

 5. In the meantime, the judgment-debtors tiled an application on 10-1-2017 praying to cancel the Boinama and to allow them to pay the decretal dues including interest. After hearing of the application, the Adalat by order dated 26-2-2017 rejected the said application and fixed the execution case for taking steps. Thereafter the judgment-debtors again filed another application on 17-4-2017 under section 57 of the Act, 2003 praying to allow the entire decretal dues by the judgment-debtors and to dispose of the execution case. 

 7. Mr Ahsanul Karim, learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that as highest bidder, the petitioner purchased the property in auction on 26-2-2013 and thereafter the Boinama was registered on 28-6-2013. Thus the sale became absolute and the execution proceeding was disposed of under section 33(9) of the Act. 2003. Long after thereof, the auction was set-aside without pointing out any illegality in the auction process. He further submits that on the ground of non-delivery of possession of auction sold property, the Adalat treated the execution case pending and set-aside the auction sale and registered Boinama on misconception of law as well as on facts. In support of his submission, learned Advocate refers to the case of Sonali Bank, Sadarghat Corporate Branch, Dhaka vs Mrs. Hazera Islam and others, reported in VI ADC 975; Sonali Bank vs Anita Adalat & others, reported in 62 DLR (AD) 231; Feroza Begum vs Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, Dhaka and others, reported in 2016 BLD (AD) 31; Mohan mad Golam Azam vs The Government of Bangladesh and others, reported in X ADC 417; Sk. Mohiuddin vs Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. 3, Dhaka and others, reported in 13 MLR (AD) 356. 

 8. By filing Affidavit-in-opposition, Mr Mohammad Mosfequs Salehin, learned Advocate for the respondents No. 4-11 contends that as per -direction of the Adalat the judgment-debtors paid entire decretal dues with up-to-date interest considering which the Adalat interfered with the auction sale observing that the auction sold property was the judgment-debtors only livelihood. He further contends that since possession of the property was not delivered to the auction-purchaser the Adalat had the jurisdiction to interfere with the auction sale. He also submits that the property was sold in a very low price and, as such, for ends of justice the auction sale was interfered. In support of his submissions, learned Advocate refers to the unreported decision, passed in the case of Md Moklesur Rahman and another vs Government of Bangladesh and others, being Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2125 of 2010; the case of Jahangir Kabir Chowdhury vs Bangladesh Government, reported in 22 BLC (AD) 139. 

 9. We have gone through the writ petition, affidavit-in-opposition filed by the respondents No.4-1I and other materials on record including the cited cases. 

 12. In the circumstances, question arises as to whether the Adalat has passed the impugned order in accordance with law setting aside the auction sale while immediately after approving the auction sale by the Adalat, the execution case was disposed of by the order dated 26-2-2013 although possession could not be handed over to the auction purchaser. 

 17. We have also gone through the cited cases, in particular, in the case of Somali Bank, Sadarghat Corporate Branch, Dhaka vs Mrs. Hazera Islam and others, reported in VI ADC 975 the Apex Court held as under: 

 "7. It appears that the decree of foreclosure in favour of the plaintiff attained its finality and the judgment debtor shall have no right to redeem the said mortgaged property. Moreover after issuance of the certificate under section 33(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain the same court of Artha Rin Adalat had no power to entertain the application of the appellant invoking section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain as such power under section 57 is only available when the other provisions of the Ain are not exhaustive. In this case after the certificate issued under section 33(5) of the Ain the decree-holder has already sold the suit property in favour of the respondent No. 8, Md Rafique by registered sale deed and therefore there is no scope to interfere with the bonafide purchase for value." 

 18. In the case reported in 62 DLR (AD) 231 the Appellate Division held as under: "5. We have perused the writ petition as well as the order dated 2-1-2005 and 9-1-2005 passed in Mortgage Execution Case No. 8 of 1995 and the Judgment and order passed in the writ petition and considered the submission made by the learned Advocate appearing for the leave petitioner. It appears that the leave petitioner bank is negligent in not informing the executing Court about the fact of restoration of the rule and stay dated 15-6-2006 and that the leave petitioner bank by filing an application on 25-6-2006 prayed for receiving the pay order submitted by the auction purchaser in Court and it appears from the impugned judgment and order passed by the High court Division that the leave petitioner bank has already encashed the pay order and thereby accepted the auction sale. In view of the provision of law to the effect that once an auction sale is complete no relief is available against such auction sale but the mortgagee may proceed against the mortgagor bank for any compensation, if it is proved that there was illegality in the auction sale. In the instant case, it is not such case rather it appears that at the instance of the decree-holder-bank auction was held and ultimately the decree-holder-bank has withdrawn the money deposited by the auction purchasers. After the auction process is completed, proceeding with the execution case is redundant. Thus we do not find any illegality in the impugned judgment passed by the High Court Division." 

 19. The Artha Rin Adalat on misconception of law interfered with the auction, on plea of non delivery of possession in favour of auction purchaser. Inasmuch as pursuant to section 5(4) of the Act, 2003 .and the above mentioned ratio of our Apex Court, after auction sale there was no scope to redeem the mortgage property. If delivery of possession through Adalat is required, the Adalat only takes step in this regard in exercising authority under sub-sections (7ka) and (7kha) of section 33 of the Act, 2003. In this regard we also find the following decision of our Apex Court i.e. the case of Feroza Begum vs Artha Rin Adalat No. 4. Dhaka and others reported in 2016 BLD (AD) 31 relevant portion of which are as follows: 

 "4. Mr Syed Mahbubar Rahman, learned Advocate-on-Record appearing on behalf of the petitioner submitted that since the delivery of possession of mortgaged property was not handed over to the decree holder bank, and the Bank has not yet submitted title documents under section 33(7)(Kha) as per order of the Artho Rin Adalat dated 5-6-2011, as such the Artho Jari Case is still pending, and not yet disposed of. The Artho Rin Adalat wrongly observed that since the Artho Jari Case is disposed of in full satisfaction there is no scope to deposit money under section 49(1) of the Ain without considering the scope of section 49(1) of the Ain. He further submitted that as per order dated 18-5-2011 the petitioner asked to deposit the loan money, accordingly he dposited Taka 50,000 this aspect of the matter was not considered by the Artha Rin Adalat or the Hon'ble Court Division. Thus the impugned judgment passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set-aside. 

 5. Mr Shamim Khaled Ahmed, learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent No. 2 made submissions in support of the impugned judgment of the High Court Division. He submitted that after the issuance of certificate under section 33 (7) of the Ain in respect of the mortgaged property, the execution case was disposed of in full satisfaction of the decree. The bank armed with the certificate, on 25-4-2011 applied for issuance of warrant for delivery of possession. He submitted that at that time the writ petitioner did not have any right to apply to cancel the certificate issued under section 33(7) and for the privilege of payment of the decretal amount by instalments under section 49 (1) of the Ain. 

 8. In the facts and circumstances described above, it is clear that the Artho Jari case is no longer pending and has in fact been properly disposed of and hence the writ petition was misconceived. In view of the foregoing, we do not find any illegality or impropriety in the impugned judgment. Accordingly, the civil petition for leave to appeal is dismissed, without, however, any order as to costs." 

 21. The unreported case cited by Mr Mohammad Mosfequs Salehin of the Appellate Division is not applicable in this case because in that particular case the apex Court has exercised the authority under article 104 of the Constitution which does not have to this Court. Similarly, in the case reported in 22 BLC (AD) 139 the apex Court set-aside the auction sale finding fraud and false representation in the auction process. But in this case, the judgment-debtors did not allege any fraud or irregularities in the auction process. Although, Mr Salehin at the fag end of his submission raised that the property was sold at shockingly low price but his two applications filed earlier before the Adalat do not reflect such allegation. 

 22. Regard being had to the above, we are of the view that the Artha Rin Adalat on misconception of law and facts passed the impugned order which warrants interference by this Court under its judicial review under Article 102 of the Constitution. Thus, the Rule Niii finds merit. 

 24. The impugned order being No. 146 dated 27-9-2017 passed by the learned Judge of Artha Rin Adalat, Lalmonirhat in Artha Rin Decree Execution Case. No. 17 of 2003 arising out of Artha Rin Suit No. 17 of 2000 (Annexure-H series) cancelling registered Boinama Deed No. 2409 dated 20-6-2013 executed and registered in the name of the petitioner with a direction upon Respondent No. 2 to make entry in Balam Bohi regarding cancellation of aforesaid Boinama Deed and also directing the petitioner to take return of BD (Bank Draft) are hereby declared to have been passed without lawful authority and if of no legal effect.
